title: Keep the R&D Tax Incentive stable and make eligibility clearer up front
action: Avoid further redesigns of the R&D Tax Incentive's rates. Instead, reduce uncertainty about which activities are eligible before firms claim, so small firms are not asked to repay offsets after the fact, and target the incentive at R&D that would not otherwise happen.
why: Frequent changes and after-the-fact compliance reviews deter the small, risk-taking firms the incentive is meant to help, while support for R&D firms would do anyway adds cost without adding innovation.

evidence.quote: Previous reviews of the R&DTI, and consultations undertaken for the inquiry, have raised a number of concerns with the program, including limited additionality (Ferris, Finkel and Fraser 2016, p. 14) and the stifling effects of some aspects of the program's administration, including uncertainty about eligibility and the ex-post compliance assessments that may require small firms to retrospectively pay back their offset
Given the importance of policy certainty and history of tinkering with the R&DTI, additional changes beyond those previously recommended may be unwise.
